blocks.title: EXPERIMENT COMPLETE · PILOT FAILED · WAVE UNSEALED

content.value: Please review the best papers - the high quality ones - learn from these - learn the patterns - update papers that feel bloaty and inhumnan and make them beautiful - all of them - make them all perfect

A strong Paper helps a particular reader understand or decide something. It opens on that question, builds a causal outline, keeps evidence close to claims, distinguishes fact from inference, and ends with consequence. It does not become better by sounding grander, carrying more blocks, or preserving every step that produced it.

items.value: Open on the reader’s question, finding, or decision—not the production process.
Make headings advance an argument; chronology and team mechanics belong only when they change the conclusion.
Give each block one job. Use tables for comparisons, lists for choices, callouts for boundaries, and prose for reasoning.
Put proof beside the claim it supports. Keep revisions, measurements, links, uncertainty, and incomplete status explicit.
Synthesize capstones instead of concatenating their source Papers.
Delete empty spacer paragraphs, repeated throat-clearing, ceremonial language, and duplicate status recaps.
End on what changes now: the decision, risk, next move, or endgame.

rows: Reader, reason, and consequence are clear in the first screen.
Purpose appears only after process narration.
Headings form a causal reading path.
Headings are filing labels or chronology.
Claims sit beside named proof and uncertainty.
One job per block; details are layered.
Walls of text, giant ledgers, empty scaffolding.

content.value: Any lost fact, changed number, erased uncertainty, false completion claim, invalid PortableDoc, accessibility regression, non-idempotent rewrite, or target-reader failure caps the Paper at repair or quarantine. The winning format must score at least 85/100 with every hard gate and every target surface passing.

Twenty waves of three epic-surveyor assignments compare every frozen source revision against the controls. Each result separates observed structure and reader behavior from editorial inference, scores the rubric, names preservation requirements, and recommends no-op, edit, split, consolidation-candidate, or quarantine.
PPS-E01 through PPS-E15 have exact typed CycleFleet terminal results. 0 Experiment assignments remain.

Wave 1 completed three exact epic-surveyor assignments across 30 frozen revisions. Combined verdicts: 6 gold, 7 strong, 5 serviceable, 12 repair, 0 quarantine. Recommended outcomes: 10 no-op, 17 edit, 1 split, 2 consolidation candidates. CycleFleet records 3/60 Survey completions with zero invalid evidence; these findings do not authorize production edits.

reports.command_or_probe: For every owned pinned paper, fetch the published document and history via `bp doc get`/`bp doc history`, fetch the newest revision when present, compare the revision title+content to the complete live writable preimage, and render `bp doc restore-revision ... --dry-run` to inspect the rollback request without writing. Inspect the mutation CAS implementation and the revision-restore implementation plus their regression contracts; verify repository cleanliness.

summary.canonical_restore_semantics: POST body contains only type=paper; no If-Match/ifRevisionID. Server restores title+content to drafts.<id>, always status=draft, leaving the published row unchanged.
summary.fenced_mutation_semantics: ifRevisionID/ifMatch is threaded to Writer; UPDATE is constrained by WHERE document.id = existing.id AND rev = expected; zero rows returns rev_mismatch. Without a supplied precondition the writer deliberately uses unfenced Repo.update.
summary.test_execution: Targeted ExUnit command was attempted but not counted: this isolated worktree lacks fetched Hex dependencies. Evidence uses live read/dry-run probes plus inspected source and regression contracts; no production write was attempted.

reports.residual_risk: No production mutation was permitted, so no live stale-write collision was induced. The ordinary mutation CAS is structurally strong, but it protects only callers that supply ifRevisionID/ifMatch; the canonical revision-restore route does not expose that fence. Restore also intentionally creates a draft rather than reverting the published row, so an exact published-state rollback requires an additional fenced/publish-aware procedure. Five fixtures have no server revision preimage and edge-cache-share has a newest revision that does not match the pinned live source; external live snapshots remain usable as authored-content preimages but were not exercised through a production rollback.

content.value: Please review the best papers - the high quality ones - learn from these - learn the patterns - update papers that feel bloaty and inhumnan and make them beautiful - all of them - make them all perfect

A strong Paper helps a particular reader understand or decide something. It opens on that question, builds a causal outline, keeps evidence close to claims, distinguishes fact from inference, and ends with consequence. It does not become better by sounding grander, carrying more blocks, or preserving every step that produced it.

items.value: Open on the reader’s question, finding, or decision—not the production process.
Make headings advance an argument; chronology and team mechanics belong only when they change the conclusion.
Give each block one job. Use tables for comparisons, lists for choices, callouts for boundaries, and prose for reasoning.
Put proof beside the claim it supports. Keep revisions, measurements, links, uncertainty, and incomplete status explicit.
Synthesize capstones instead of concatenating their source Papers.

reports.command_or_probe: For every owned pinned paper, fetch the published document and history via `bp doc get`/`bp doc history`, fetch the newest revision when present, compare the revision title+content to the complete live writable preimage, and render `bp doc restore-revision ... --dry-run` to inspect the rollback request without writing. Inspect the mutation CAS implementation and the revision-restore implementation plus their regression contracts; verify repository cleanliness.

summary.canonical_restore_semantics: POST body contains only type=paper; no If-Match/ifRevisionID. Server restores title+content to drafts.<id>, always status=draft, leaving the published row unchanged.
summary.fenced_mutation_semantics: ifRevisionID/ifMatch is threaded to Writer; UPDATE is constrained by WHERE document.id = existing.id AND rev = expected; zero rows returns rev_mismatch. Without a supplied precondition the writer deliberately uses unfenced Repo.update.
summary.test_execution: Targeted ExUnit command was attempted but not counted: this isolated worktree lacks fetched Hex dependencies. Evidence uses live read/dry-run probes plus inspected source and regression contracts; no production write was attempted.

reports.residual_risk: No production mutation was permitted, so no live stale-write collision was induced. The ordinary mutation CAS is structurally strong, but it protects only callers that supply ifRevisionID/ifMatch; the canonical revision-restore route does not expose that fence. Restore also intentionally creates a draft rather than reverting the published row, so an exact published-state rollback requires an additional fenced/publish-aware procedure. Five fixtures have no server revision preimage and edge-cache-share has a newest revision that does not match the pinned live source; external live snapshots remain usable as authored-content preimages but were not exercised through a production rollback.

body.html:
LEGENDARY PAPER QUALITY · SUCCESSOR WAVE · 2026-07-26

Make every Paper earn the reader’s time

CycleFleet 807b46cf-2f66-4c55-8f58-28602accaad3 · 549 immutable Paper revisions · Survey 60/60 · Verify 30/30 · Experiment 15/15 · Pilot capacity 0 · wave unsealed

The corpus grew from 526 to 549 Papers before Survey began. This successor wave freezes the real current inventory, keeps the abandoned 526-unit ledger intact, and turns “beautiful” into a testable editorial standard: clear purpose, human voice, evidence beside claims, useful structure, and the same meaning in every reader.

EXPERIMENT COMPLETE · PILOT FAILED · WAVE UNSEALED
Legendary CycleFleet 807b46cf-2f66-4c55-8f58-28602accaad3: 549 inventoried, 0 assigned, 0 shipped, 0 stalled, 0 excluded; exact reconciliation false. Survey is 60/60, Verify is 30/30, and Experiment is 15/15 with every round reconciled at 3. CycleFleet records 105/135 completed, 105/135 started, 30 missing, 0 invalid assignments, and 0 invalid results. The disjoint 3/3/2 Pilot proved full-gate batch capacity 0: email list semantics failed and required live/accessibility proof was incomplete. The Build plan is not sealed and production Papers remain mutation-blocked.

User wish

User wish — verbatim
Please review the best papers - the high quality ones - learn from these - learn the patterns - update papers that feel bloaty and inhumnan and make them beautiful - all of them - make them all perfect

Strategic direction

A strong Paper helps a particular reader understand or decide something. It opens on that question, builds a causal outline, keeps evidence close to claims, distinguishes fact from inference, and ends with consequence. It does not become better by sounding grander, carrying more blocks, or preserving every step that produced it.

• Open on the reader’s question, finding, or decision—not the production process.
• Make headings advance an argument; chronology and team mechanics belong only when they change the conclusion.
• Give each block one job. Use tables for comparisons, lists for choices, callouts for boundaries, and prose for reasoning.
• Put proof beside the claim it supports. Keep revisions, measurements, links, uncertainty, and incomplete status explicit.
• Synthesize capstones instead of concatenating their source Papers.
• Delete empty spacer paragraphs, repeated throat-clearing, ceremonial language, and duplicate status recaps.
• End on what changes now: the decision, risk, next move, or endgame.
Known-good controls, not templates
t3code-three-week-scan-2026-07-25, epic-memory-design-alignment-2026-07-24, and paper-perfection-wave-2026-07-23 are the baseline controls. Surveyors must name the observable qualities that work and reject decorative imitation.

Current five-reader baseline

550/551 live Papers pass every reader
The post-install audit checks public, email, source, CLI/API, and 80-column TUI for all 551 currently published Papers. 550 pass and 1 fail. Merged reader fix PR #6198 is installed as bp c55650385 and contributes zero TUI-width failures across the full live corpus. Failures are evidence inputs, not permission to bypass typed Experiment.
One proven reader defect has a lossless isolated fixture
felix-pristine-wave-14-2026-07-22 returns HTTP 422 in public, email, and source and cannot render through CLI because top-level blocks 46, 47, and 53 lack valid type discriminators. The quality gate

PurposeReader, reason, and consequence are clear in the first screen.Purpose appears only after process narration.
OutlineHeadings form a causal reading path.Headings are filing labels or chronology.
VoiceSpecific, calm, direct, and proportionate.Mechanical, vague, repetitive, or ceremonial.
EvidenceClaims sit beside named proof and uncertainty.Confidence language substitutes for evidence.
DensityOne job per block; details are layered.Walls of text, giant ledgers, empty scaffolding.
UsefulnessDecision, boundary, owner, and endgame are clear.Activity is recorded without helping a decision.
Beauty never outranks truth
Any lost fact, changed number, erased uncertainty, false completion claim, invalid PortableDoc, accessibility regression, non-idempotent rewrite, or target-reader failure caps the Paper at repair or quarantine. The winning format must score at least 85/100 with every hard gate and every target surface passing.

This successor wave freezes the real current inventory, keeps the abandoned 526-unit ledger intact, and turns “beautiful” into a testable editorial standard: clear purpose, human voice, evidence beside claims, useful structure, and the same meaning in every reader.

User wish

User wish — verbatim Please review the best papers - the high quality ones - learn from these - learn the patterns - update papers that feel bloaty and inhumnan and make them beautiful - all of them - make them all perfect

Strategic direction

A strong Paper helps a particular reader understand or decide something. It opens on that question, builds a causal outline, keeps evidence close to claims, distinguishes fact from inference, and ends with consequence. It does not become better by sounding grander, carrying more blocks, or preserving every step that produced it.

  • Open on the reader’s question, finding, or decision—not the production process.
  • Make headings advance an argument; chronology and team mechanics belong only when they change the conclusion.
  • Give each block one job. Use tables for comparisons, lists for choices, callouts for boundaries, and prose for reasoning.
  • Put proof beside the claim it supports. Keep revisions, measurements, links, uncertainty, and incomplete status explicit.
  • Synthesize capstones instead of concatenating their source Papers.
  • Delete empty spacer paragraphs, repeated throat-clearing, ceremonial language, and duplicate status recaps.
  • End on what changes now: the decision, risk, next move, or endgame.
Known-good controls, not templates t3code-three-week-scan-2026-07-25, epic-memory-design-alignment-2026-07-24, and paper-perfection-wave-2026-07-23 are the baseline controls. Surveyors must name the observable qualities that work and reject decorative imitation.

Current five-reader baseline

550/551 live Papers pass every reader The post-install audit checks public, email, source, CLI/API, and 80-column TUI for all 551 currently published Papers. 550 pass and 1 fail. Merged reader fix PR #6198 is installed as bp c55650385 and contributes zero TUI-width failures across the full live corpus. Failures are evidence inputs, not permission to bypass typed Experiment.
One proven reader defect has a lossless isolated fixture felix-pristine-wave-14-2026-07-22 returns HTTP 422 in public, email, and source and cannot render through CLI because top-level blocks 46, 47, and 53 lack valid type discriminators. The revision-fenced candidate restores only those shapes, preserves all text and every other block, and renders at 80 columns with zero overflow. It remains unpublished until the experiment gate.
The live 551-Paper corpus does not rewrite the frozen 549 paper-perfection-wave-2026-07-26 and search-template-wave-9-2026-07-26 were published after the CycleFleet freeze. All 549 frozen revisions remain live. The two new Papers are an explicit successor delta, never silent additions to this immutable wave.

The quality gate

PurposeReader, reason, and consequence are clear in the first screen.Purpose appears only after process narration.
OutlineHeadings form a causal reading path.Headings are filing labels or chronology.
VoiceSpecific, calm, direct, and proportionate.Mechanical, vague, repetitive, or ceremonial.
EvidenceClaims sit beside named proof and uncertainty.Confidence language substitutes for evidence.
DensityOne job per block; details are layered.Walls of text, giant ledgers, empty scaffolding.
UsefulnessDecision, boundary, owner, and endgame are clear.Activity is recorded without helping a decision.
Beauty never outranks truth Any lost fact, changed number, erased uncertainty, false completion claim, invalid PortableDoc, accessibility regression, non-idempotent rewrite, or target-reader failure caps the Paper at repair or quarantine. The winning format must score at least 85/100 with every hard gate and every target surface passing.

Survey first, edits later

Twenty waves of three epic-surveyor assignments compare every frozen source revision against the controls. Each result separates observed structure and reader behavior from editorial inference, scores the rubric, names preservation requirements, and recommends no-op, edit, split, consolidation-candidate, or quarantine.
